title: KVCache: checksum-based corruption alerts and eviction-throttle remediation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: During a capacity surge on 2026-02-18 we observed intermittent incorrect values being served from the KV cache for live inference requests. The issue manifested as stale or garbled prefix values for a subset of models, causing elevated error rates and retries that amplified load. This ticket tracks the follow-up work: introduce lightweight checksum-based detection, an eviction-throttle circuit breaker to avoid eviction storms, a controlled rehydrate path for suspect keys, improved telemetry, and testing to prevent regressions.

Impact: customer-facing increased 5xxs for some tenants and a 12% tail latency increase during the event window. No data loss, but degraded quality for serving outputs and higher infra cost due to retries.

Root cause hypothesis (current): a race between concurrent eviction and insert paths produced partially-written slab entries under rare timing and compaction timing combinations on machines with high fragmentation. These partial writes were not always detected by the existing index validation because some header flags were set inconsistently during the crashy race.

Goals: 1) Detect corrupted entries quickly in production with minimal cost; 2) Throttle eviction activity during noisy recovery windows to avoid amplification; 3) Provide deterministic offline sweep/rehydration job to repair state without full node restart; 4) Add unit/integration tests and chaos harnesses to prevent regressions.

Success criteria (measurable): 1) New checksum alerts fire within 30s of first corrupted entry; 2) Eviction-throttle prevents eviction rate from exceeding safe RPS for 95% of noisy windows; 3) Runbook for automatic rehydrate completes within SLO (no more than 2x normal latency for affected keys); 4) No related incidents in the next 3 months under comparable load.
activity: 2026-02-20 - Ticket created by Ava Chen: initial triage notes and incident link. Assigned to Marcus Li for lead investigation.

2026-02-21 - Investigation: reproduced partial-write pattern on local stress harness by combining concurrent eviction + compaction + GC window. Hypothesis: write path doesn't serialise header-flag updates with slab allocation in rare interleavings.

2026-02-23 - Decision: immediate mitigations prioritized over full redesign. Two parallel tracks: (A) detection + alerting (checksum) to catch corrupted entries; (B) operational throttle to slow eviction during ramp/warmup to reduce race exposure.

2026-02-25 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/kvcache/pull/1892 implements a 64-bit xxHash checksum in entry header and a fast validation path in Get(). Marcus Li authored; code under feature flag 'kvc_checksum_v1'.

2026-02-27 - QA: checksum flag tested under regression harness; observed ~0.6% CPU overhead at 99th percentile on 1k qps synthetic workload. Performance trade-off accepted for deployment behind flag and sampling (1/1000) by default.

2026-03-01 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/kvcache/pull/1897 implements 'eviction-throttle' - circuit that monitors local eviction rate and backs off eviction workers when node-wide eviction RPS exceeds configured threshold. Includes metrics 'kvc.eviction.rps' and 'kvc.eviction.throttle_ratio'.
2026-03-03 - Ops: rolled out checksum sampling to canary region (us-west-2) with sample_rate=1/1000. No alerts triggered after 48h. Preparing to increase sample_rate to 1/100 for next week.

2026-03-04 - Review notes from reliability team (Diego Patel): request to add an adaptive sample ramp to avoid cold-start blind spots. Action: add sample-rate ramp based on node uptime and cache fill fraction. Marcus updated PR with ramp logic.

2026-03-06 - Runbook draft created: docs/internal/runbooks/kvc_cache_rehydrate.md — includes steps to isolate node, enable throttles, run rehydrate sweep, monitor 'kvc.checksum.failures' and fallback to previous model variant if needed.

2026-03-07 - Load test: chaos run against staging cluster (50k qps) with compaction stress caused 7 deterministic header-corruption events; checksum detected 6/7 under sample_rate=1/100 and 7/7 when sample_rate=1/10. Eviction-throttle prevented eviction storm: eviction RPS stayed under configured ceiling and downstream 5xxs did not spike.
2026-03-08 - Security review: no PII in checksums. KMS not required. Security sign-off from Olivia Grant for the checksum telemetry path.

2026-03-09 - Deployment plan: incrementally enable checksum sample_rate to 1/100 in all regions over 72 hours, enable eviction-throttle with soft limits, and add alert 'kvc.checksum.alert' for >5 failures in 1m. Estimated rollout time: 3 days.

2026-03-10 - Next steps assigned: Marcus to merge PRs after final perf review; QA to add deterministic failure tests to CI; Observability (Lena Rodriguez) to add dashboards and pager rules. Blockers: finalize safe default thresholds for eviction-throttle (see dependency ENG-61421 for historic thresholds).
